# Sercha

> Sercha turns an organisation's data (connected systems, landed tables,
> documents) into tables you query with SerchaQL, a SQL dialect that reads like
> PostgreSQL. Every query runs as the caller and returns only rows the caller
> is granted.

What you can read with SerchaQL:

- **Model entities and relations**, by bare name (`FROM Customer c`), walked
  with `JOIN <relation> r ON r.from_key = c.key`.
- **Landed tables** as `tables.<source>.<table>`, and their normalised form as
  `clean.<source>.<table>`.
- **Datasets** as `data.<table>`, also as of a past time with `AS OF`.
- **Entities extracted from documents** as `<corpus>.<Entity>`, linked with
  `JOIN ... VIA`.
- **Saved views and materialized views**, by name.

Statements run through `POST /api/v1/query`. Agents connect over MCP and can
call `describe serchaql` for the same language reference these pages hold.

## Docs

- [What SerchaQL is](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/intro): what you can read and how.
- [Querying](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/dml): every clause and function, refused forms with what to write instead, SHOW.
- [Defining](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/ddl): the model, views, tools, named edges, people, access, document extraction.
- [Removed and reserved](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/changes): forms older versions accepted.
- [API](https://docs.sercha.dev/api/sercha-api): tokens, query, saved tools, catalogue, sources, documents, exports.
